title: Man'yōshū
description: Position 4 in the owner-supplied audited revision. Attribution: Many poets; compilation uncertain, with Ōtomo no Yakamochi traditionally associated with its final formation. Date: 8th-century compilation; latest dated poem 759. Form: Collective poetry anthology. The diversity of voices, occasions and poetic scales gives this anthology exceptional range. It rises because an all-form canon should recognize poetry's foundational imaginative achievement alongside the later novel.

title: Kokin Wakashū
description: Position 11 in the owner-supplied audited revision. Attribution: Many poets; compilers Ki no Tsurayuki, Ki no Tomonori, Ōshikōchi no Mitsune and Mibu no Tadamine. Date: commissioned 905; completed in the early 10th century. Form: Imperial waka anthology and poetics. The ordered anthology makes seasons and love into extended structures of feeling. Its importance lies in arrangement and critical self-definition as well as individual poems, justifying a substantial rise from the original list.

title: Shin Kokin Wakashū
description: Position 25 in the owner-supplied audited revision. Attribution: Many poets; Emperor Go-Toba supervised appointed compilers Minamoto no Michitomo, Fujiwara no Ariie, Fujiwara no Teika, Fujiwara no Ietaka, Fujiwara no Masatsune and Jakuren, who died before completion. Date: 1205 initial presentation; continued revisions. Form: Imperial waka anthology. Allusion, sequence and suggestive incompleteness produce a poetic world distinct from the Kokinshū. This addition recognizes the anthology as an artistic construction and a major transformation of inherited poetic language.
